title: Mondovi Got Its Name From Napoleon's Battlefield in Italy
summary: A Wisconsin Magazine of History account traces Mondovi's unusual name to pioneer Elihu B. Gifford. While reading about the Napoleonic wars, Gifford encountered the name Mondovi—the site of Napoleon's 1796 victory in northwestern Italy—and applied it to the Wisconsin settlement on Beef River.

title: Before It Was Mondovi, French Traders Called This the Beef River
summary: The river running through the future Mondovi area was known to early French traders as Rivière de Boeuf—literally Beef River. The English name Buffalo River later became standard.

title: A 1877 Bird's-Eye Map Captured Tiny Mondovi From an Imaginary Sky
summary: Long before aerial photography, cartographers drew a detailed bird's-eye view of Mondovi as though seen from above. The 1877 panorama survives in the Wisconsin Historical Society collection and records the young village's streets and buildings.

title: Mondovi's Rural History Museum Preserves an Entire One-Room Schoolhouse
summary: The Mondovi Area Historical Society preserves a restored one-room country schoolhouse interpreting how children in the surrounding farm country were educated before consolidated schools became standard.

title: Mondovi Preserves a Historic Farmstead, Barn and Outbuildings
summary: The Mondovi Area Historical Society's Olson Farm Museum preserves a farmhouse, barn and outbuildings as a surviving example of the agricultural life that shaped the countryside around Mondovi.

title: Mondovi's Railroad Line Was Eventually Turned Into a Trail
summary: The Omaha Railroad branch eventually linked Fairchild, Osseo, Strum, Eleva and Mondovi. The line was abandoned in 1975, and its former right-of-way later became an all-purpose recreational trail.

title: Mondovi's Largest Lake Is Only About 44 Acres
summary: Buffalo County is a landscape of rivers and trout streams rather than large inland lakes. Mirror Lake at Mondovi is the county's largest named lake, yet covers only about 44 acres.

title: A 1901 Beaux-Arts Commercial Building Still Anchors Downtown Mondovi
summary: A substantial two-story commercial building erected in 1901 survives in Mondovi with its large frieze, cornice and parapet still visible. The Wisconsin Historical Society classifies its architecture as Neoclassical/Beaux Arts.

title: Osseo Burned in a Major 1881 Fire
summary: A major fire swept through Osseo in 1881. The Trempealeau County Historical Society preserves both documentation of the disaster and imagery of downtown from before the fire, making the event a defining break in the town's early history.

title: Photographs Preserve What Downtown Osseo Looked Like Before It Burned
summary: The Trempealeau County Historical Society preserves an image of downtown Osseo dating from before the catastrophic 1881 fire, offering a rare visual record of buildings and streets that were subsequently lost.

title: The Railroad Reached Osseo in June 1887
summary: The Fairchild & Mississippi railroad project pushed west from Fairchild and reached Osseo on June 20, 1887. The connection became the beginning of the branch that later continued through Strum and Eleva toward Mondovi.

title: Osseo Was 14.21 Railroad Miles From Fairchild
summary: The new railroad measured the Fairchild-to-Osseo segment at 14.21 miles. Osseo became the first major western destination before construction continued toward Strum, Eleva and eventually Mondovi.

title: Osseo's Railroad Began as the Fairchild & Mississippi Railway
summary: The company behind Osseo's rail connection was organized in 1886 as the Fairchild & Mississippi Railway Company. Before the tracks even reached Osseo, stockholders renamed it the Sault Ste. Marie & Southwestern Railway Company.

title: A Railroad From Osseo Eventually Connected Four Small Western Wisconsin Towns
summary: After reaching Osseo in 1887, the branch pushed west to Strum, Eleva and Mondovi. The route tied a string of small agricultural communities to the larger regional rail network.

title: Osseo High School Once Advertised for Students
summary: A surviving 1914 advertisement promoted Osseo's high school to prospective students. At a time when attending high school was still optional, schools could actively compete to attract young people.

title: Osseo Had an Organized Girls' Basketball Team by 1920
summary: The Trempealeau County Historical Society preserves a photograph of Osseo's 1920 girls' basketball team, documenting organized girls' athletics in the community more than a century ago.

title: Osseo's Old High School Was Vacated in 1917
summary: Historical Society collections identify Osseo's old high school as having been vacated in 1917. A town hall was temporarily used by sixth- and seventh-grade students until it too was vacated that April.

title: Osseo's Rural Countryside Was Dotted With One-Room Schools
summary: Historical collections around Osseo document numerous rural schools—including Golden Valley, Kings Valley, South Valley, Pine Creek and Tracey Valley—showing how education was once distributed among tiny neighborhood school districts.

title: A Man Remembered as the 'Learned Hermit' Lived Near Osseo
summary: Trempealeau County historical collections preserve the story of Nicholas Bourlier, remembered locally as the 'Learned Hermit' of Kings Valley, a distinctive figure in the rural countryside near Osseo.
location: Kings Valley near Osseo, Trempealeau County

title: Osseo's Railroad to Mondovi Vanished in 1975
summary: The railroad branch that had connected Osseo westward through Strum and Eleva to Mondovi since the nineteenth century was abandoned in 1975. The old transportation corridor later found a new life as a recreational trail.
